index.title: hush: feedback and anonymous tracking for your apps
index.description: Self-hosted in-app feedback, anonymous usage tracking and remote config for mobile and web apps. One container, Postgres, a dashboard and an SDK on npm (@bavrk/hush). No IP addresses, no consent banner. MIT.

hero.lead: In-app feedback and anonymous usage tracking for mobile and web apps. One small container, Postgres, a dashboard and an SDK on npm. No account, no IP address, nothing to ask consent for.
hero.note: Built for our own apps and running in production there. Shared as-is.
hero.screenAlt: The hush dashboard: an app's active installs per day, sessions, a paywall funnel, retention and versions

how.s1_p: Run docker compose with the example in the repo: one container and a Postgres beside it, on your own server.
how.s2_p: Install @bavrk/hush from npm in your Expo, React Native, web or Capacitor app, give it the server's URL and a write key, and call init().
how.s3_p: The dashboard shows installs, sessions, retention and your own events, the feedback inbox where you reply, and the remote config you change without a release.

features.h2: Feedback, usage and remote config on one server
features.f1_p: Users write from inside the app: a problem, an idea, or kind words. You answer on the dashboard (and by email, if they left one); they read it in the app and can reply.
features.f2_p: A random install id is the only identifier. No IP address is stored anywhere, and nothing personal is collected, so there is no consent banner.
features.f3_p: Installs, sessions, retention and cohorts, ordered funnels with the time between steps, your own events broken down by any prop, and where installs came from: campaign links, App Store campaigns and Apple's ad attribution.
features.f4_p: Flags, kill switches, numbers and copy the app reads at runtime, declared in the catalog and changed on the dashboard without a release. Targeting and rollouts are worked out on the device, which reports nothing back.
features.f5_p: Optionally, RevenueCat's own figures on the same page, pulled by your server with a read-only key.
features.f6_p: One container and Postgres on your own server. Your users' data never passes through anyone else.
features.f7_h: An SDK that stays out of the way
features.f7_p: @bavrk/hush on npm, for Expo, React Native, the web and Capacitor, and a Swift package for native iOS apps. Queues offline, sends in batches, and survives being killed. If the server is down, the app behaves exactly as without it.
features.f8_p: A Claude Code plugin, and a skill for Cursor, Codex and other agents, add hush to your app, plan its events and funnels, and answer questions about it, following the rules on the docs page.

collected.h2: What hush stores, and what it never does
collected.yes1: A random install id the app creates; deleting the app deletes it
collected.yes2: App version, OS, device model and the device's language
collected.yes3: The events and props your app sends (what the app did, not who did it)
collected.yes4: Feedback messages, and an email address only if a user typed one
collected.yes5: Country, only if you enable it behind a trusted proxy
collected.no1: IP addresses, in the database or anywhere else
collected.no4: Raw events past the retention window (180 days by default)
collected.no5: Your users' data on any server but yours

privacy.short: This website sets no cookies and runs no analytics. The server keeps a short request log for security. hush, the software, collects no personal data from app users; its own privacy model is at the end of this page.
privacy.s1_p: hush.bavrk.com is run by {{cfg.company}}. You can reach us at {{cfg.supportEmail}}.
privacy.s2_p: No cookies, no analytics, no tracking scripts, no embedded third-party content. Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts, which receives your IP address when your browser fetches them. Our web server keeps an access log (time, address, page, browser) for 30 days to investigate abuse, then deletes it.
privacy.s3_p: The live demo shows invented apps and data. It is read-only, stores nothing you do in it, and accepts no data from apps.
privacy.s4_p: When you run hush for your own app, you are the one collecting data and you decide what your privacy policy says. By design hush stores a random install id, the app version, OS, device model, the device's language, the events your app sends, feedback messages, an email address only if a user typed one, and a country only if you enable it. It never stores IP addresses. Remote config collects nothing: the app asks for it with its key and the revision it holds. We never see any of it: your server, your data.

terms.s2_p: hush is built for our own apps and shared as-is. It comes without warranty of any kind, as the MIT License says, and without any promise of support, updates or fitness for your purpose.
terms.s3_p: If you run hush, you operate it: you are responsible for your server, its security, your users' data and your own privacy policy. We have no access to your instance.
terms.s4_p: This website and the demo are provided for information, free of charge, and may change or go away. Please do not try to break the demo; it holds only invented data.

support.lead: hush is a tool we built for ourselves and share as-is, so help is best-effort.
support.email_label: Found a bug or have a question? Open an issue on GitHub, or email us. We read everything, and answer when we can.
support.faq1_a: The only identifier is a random install id the app creates for itself. No IP address is stored, no account exists, and no advertising id is read. An email address exists only when a user types one into feedback so you can answer them.
support.faq2_q: Can I use it for my app?
support.faq2_a: Yes. It is MIT licensed: run it on your own server, commercially too. It is built for small apps like ours: one instance, in-memory rate limits, Postgres.
support.faq3_a: No, on purpose. Your users' data stays on your server; we never see it. The live demo shows exactly what you get.
support.faq4_q: Which platforms does the SDK support?
support.faq4_a: Expo and React Native, web pages, PWAs and Capacitor, all from the npm package @bavrk/hush, with @bavrk/hush-expo and @bavrk/hush-capacitor for the native iOS side; and native Swift apps through the Hush Swift package. Its core runs on any JavaScript platform that gives it storage and app lifecycle. The API is plain HTTP and JSON, so any client can talk to it; the README documents every endpoint.
support.faq5_q: What does it cost to run?
support.faq5_a: A container using under 100 MB of memory and a small Postgres database: the smallest VPS or a corner of a server you already have.
